name: DMRadio apparatus (DMRadio-m3 / DMRadio-50L)
notes: No placements[] entry recorded: facility:slac (and any Stanford-campus site) are owned by the facilities lead and not yet landed this wave; DMRadio-50L is explicitly described as being built on the Stanford University campus itself, distinct from the SLAC site, per the cited source.

summary.plain: DMRadio is a family of experiments being built at Stanford and SLAC that use a magnet and a tuned electrical circuit, instead of a microwave cavity, to search for very light dark-matter axions.
summary.technical: Lumped-element LC-resonator axion haloscopes: DMRadio-50L (1 T toroidal magnet, 5 kHz-5 MHz) on the Stanford University campus and DMRadio-m3 (4 T solenoidal magnet, 30-200 MHz) at SLAC; under construction as of the sources fetched this session.

technology.note: No 'lumped-element' value exists in the ontology's technology_classes enum; recorded as 'other' (see worklog).
technology.value: Lumped-element resonant LC-circuit axion dark-matter search: a toroidal (DMRadio-50L) or solenoidal (DMRadio-m3) magnet coupled to a high-Q LC oscillator and SQUID readout, sensitive to sub-microwave-frequency axion-induced currents rather than a resonant cavity.
